rounds.text: Shahi Shipping Ltd demonstrates a resilient core capability to generate cash, evidenced by positive operating cash flow of Rs 0.26 Cr as of March 2026 [E32]. The company maintains a strong commitment from its leadership, with promoter holdings increasing by 22.6% over the last quarter [E43]. Despite recent volatility, the firm has proven its ability to deliver value, evidenced by a 3-year compounded share price growth of 23% [E21] and a robust 3-year median return on equity of 30% [E25]. Furthermore, the company’s ROCE of 11.8% significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of 6.61% [E9]. Conceded: [E1], [E12], [E16], [E18], [E34], [E46], [E48], [E50]. While the business operates in a cyclical environment [E41], its historical track record of a 29.7% 3-year ROE highlights an underlying operational efficiency that is currently being overlooked by the market [E42].

The bull’s reliance on positive operating cash flow [E32] ignores that the company is simultaneously burning cash on a free cash flow basis, which reached Rs -0.97 Cr in March 2026 [E33]. While promoter confidence is cited via recent share increases [E43], this must be weighed against the broader reality of a 18.68x debt-to-equity ratio that signals extreme leverage risk [E34]. The bull highlights historical 3-year ROE [E25, E42] and share price growth [E21], yet these figures are starkly contradicted by the most recent performance, where ROE has cratered to -127% [E12, E26] and annual share price growth has plummeted by 34% [E22]. Conceded: [E9], [E21], [E25], [E32], [E42], [E43]. Furthermore, the claim of operational efficiency is undermined by a 40% decline in trailing twelve-month sales [E16] and a consistent, six-quarter trend of decreasing operating margins [E30]. Ultimately, the company’s valuation remains detached from its deteriorating fundamentals, as evidenced by a P/B ratio of 30.62x [E1] that stands in stark contrast to the sector benchmark of 1.38x [E6].
